items.title: Is AEO/GEO different than SEO? Insights from AI platforms
items.summary: Glenn Gabe examines whether traditional SEO practices cover Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) by compiling statements from leaders at Google (Jeff Dean, Danny Sullivan, John Mueller, Nick Fox), Microsoft (Krishna Madhavan), and Perplexity (Jesse Dwyer). The post highlights evolving guidance on optimizing for AI search and promises updates with more direct sources. This underscores the need for SEOs to adapt beyond classic strategies.

items.title: Latest AI SEO stats to steer your 2026 strategy
items.summary: Semrush provides critical data on how AI platforms are eroding organic traffic and altering search behaviors, urging SEOs to track shifts quantitatively. The post links to a blog with the freshest statistics for planning ahead in 2026. This is essential for content marketers navigating AI-driven changes.

items.title: Open-source geo-seo-claude tool optimizes websites for AI search engines
items.summary: A new 100% open-source tool called geo-seo-claude performs full GEO audits using parallel subagents for sites targeting AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude. It delivers 60-second visibility snapshots, analyzes structured schema for LLMs, and generates PDF reports. This trending tool addresses the rise of AI search optimization needs.

items.title: Google AI Overviews cut search clicks 42%: Report
items.summary: Google’s AI Overviews are reducing organic search clicks by 42% for publishers, particularly impacting evergreen and informational content, while creating opportunities in breaking news and Google Discover for content marketing strategies. Breaking news traffic surged 103% from November 2024 through early 2026, with Discover clicks growing 30% and becoming a key growth engine as web search traffic declined. This shift emphasizes the need for real-time content optimization to leverage AI-resistant channels like news distribution.

items.title: Prompt research: The next layer of SEO and GEO strategy
items.summary: Prompt research analyzes questions asked in generative AI systems to understand how content aligns with conversational prompts, reshaping SEO and GEO by focusing on prompt patterns rather than isolated keywords. This approach expands content strategy to cover prompt clusters, including informational, comparative, and transactional queries, ensuring visibility in both traditional search and AI-generated answers. By incorporating prompt engineering, brands can optimize for evolving search behaviors that blend ranked results with conversational interactions.

items.title: AI assistants now equal 56% of global search engine volume: Study
items.summary: AI tools generate 45 billion monthly sessions worldwide, equaling 56% of global search engine volume and 34% in the U.S., with most activity driven by mobile apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, and Claude. Total usage across search engines and AI assistants has grown 26% globally since 2023, expanding discovery rather than shrinking search demand. This shift implies that SEO strategies must incorporate both traditional rankings and LLM visibility, as AI platforms account for significant search-like activity.

items.title: Author Blasts Publishing Company for Embracing AI, Calls It Against Writing's Essence
items.summary: Twitter user @wildwithabandon criticizes 7Seas publishing for using AI, stating it cannot coexist with literature as it undermines the core of writing. They demand the company better understand its market. The post received 258 likes on March 2, 2026.

items.title: BookTok Blamed for Flood of Unedited, Low-Quality Books Skipping Traditional Editing
items.summary: User @nutriculum holds BookTok responsible for poor-quality books bypassing editing, noting traditional publishers would reject such work. They call skipping editors criminal and revealing of priorities. Posted March 7, 2026, in a publishing discussion.

items.title: Children's Author Celebrates Signing Fourth and Biggest Book Deal at Age 40
items.summary: Blair N. Williamson announces her fourth and largest book deal at 40, inspiring others that age is no barrier to dreams in publishing. Shared with motivational hashtags like #noexcuses and #writingcommunity. Post from March 2, 2026, with 134 likes.

items.title: Thousands of Authors Publish 'Empty' Book to Protest AI Firms Using Their Work Without Permission
items.summary: On March 10, 2026, authors like Kazuo Ishiguro, Philippa Gregory, and Richard Osman released a blank book 'Don’t Steal This Book' listing contributors to protest AI training on their works. Organized by Ed Newton-Rex, it pressures the UK government ahead of a copyright review on March 18. The action highlights AI's threat to creators' livelihoods.

items.title: Draft2Digital Rejects Up to 75% of Submissions Due to AI-Generated Nonfiction Flood
items.summary: Draft2Digital CEO Kris Austin explains blocking dozens of nonfiction categories like health and business due to low-quality, often dangerous AI books clogging pipelines. Rejections hit 40-75%, slowing legit authors, while AI fiction fails to engage readers lacking human elements. Reported March 10, 2026.

items.title: Local Author Gemma Denham Signs Second Book Deal with Publisher
items.summary: Gemma Denham celebrates securing her second book deal, shared by CahillDavisPublishing on March 7, 2026. This milestone highlights ongoing success in traditional publishing paths. The story appeared on MSN entertainment news.

items.title: Woke ‘The Bride!’ Bombs at Box Office: Crushed by ‘Hoppers’ and Even ‘Scream 7’
items.summary: Warner Bros.' 'The Bride!', a feminist reimagining of the Bride of Frankenstein featuring themes of male oppression, non-consent, and a 'Me Too'-inspired revolution, opened to just $7.26 million across 3,304 theaters, missing projections of $16-18 million. It was outperformed by Disney/Pixar's family film 'Hoppers' ($46 million) and 'Scream 7's second weekend ($17.3 million), earning a 'C+' CinemaScore amid criticism of its heavy-handed messaging. Despite a $90 million budget and stars like Christian Bale, the film suffered from poor reviews and weak audience turnout.

items.title: British Television Journalists of Color Report Backlash Over DEI Initiatives
items.summary: Journalists of color in British television have shared experiences of resentment and backlash from white colleagues due to perceived advantages from diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts following the 2020 Black Lives Matter movement. The revelations highlight internal tensions within the industry over DEI policies. This comes amid broader discussions on the impact of such initiatives in entertainment.

items.title: 2026 Oscars: The Success of 'Sinners' Is Not 'Wokeness'
items.summary: As 'Sinners' leads Oscar predictions, including Best Actor for Michael B. Jordan, discussions arise countering claims of 'wokeness' driving its success post-2020 Academy changes aimed at diversity. The film's strong performance is attributed to merit rather than diversity mandates. This narrative challenges perceptions of Oscars favoring ideological content over quality.

items.title: Woke Crusades Persist in Hollywood Over Film Boycott Drama
items.summary: An actress celebrated a film's box office success despite a failed boycott by pro-Palestine activists, leading to backlash that prompted her apology, which was rejected. A 'queer voices' publication highlighted the story but faced criticism from its own audience for not labeling Israel’s actions as 'genocide'. The incident exemplifies ongoing internal conflicts within progressive Hollywood circles.

items.title: Taylor Sheridan’s 'Marshals' Show Starts with Woke Elements
items.summary: The new CBS series 'Marshals' from Taylor Sheridan opens with virtue-signaling to Lakota culture, criticisms of 'America' poisoning tribal water, and a U.S. Marshals team featuring two women alongside men. Viewers note the portrayal of surly family dynamics and female marshals handling high-risk fugitives as unrealistic. Sheridan’s shift draws complaints of female empowerment tropes overriding realism.

items.title: Netflix Accused of Systematic Propaganda in Content Tropes
items.summary: A viral post lists recurring Netflix tropes including villainous white men, heroic Black men, wise trans characters, mocked traditional masculinity, and dysfunctional nuclear families. It claims Netflix prioritizes social engineering over entertainment with anti-capitalist, pro-climate activism, and interracial pairing emphases. The thread resonates with audiences frustrated by predictable ideological messaging.

items.title: Launch Commerce Rebrands from Launch Cart, Unveils AI-Powered Business Platform for Small Businesses
items.summary: Launch Commerce has rebranded from Launch Cart and launched an AI-powered platform tailored for small businesses to streamline operations. The single AI system automates customer follow-ups, improves response times, and captures missed leads, addressing the challenge of juggling multiple disparate tools. This innovation aims to boost efficiency and growth for small business owners.

items.title: VistaPrint Launches Generative AI Logomaker to Simplify Branding for Small Businesses
items.summary: VistaPrint has introduced a new generative AI Logomaker enabling small businesses to create personalized logos in minutes via guided prompts and advanced editing features. Users receive free SVG, PDF, and PNG files, built on VistaPrint's expertise in design and AI. This tool democratizes professional branding, saving time and costs for entrepreneurs.

items.title: Micro Launches Open Beta of AI-Native Workspace Merging CRM and Email for Small Teams
items.summary: Micro announced the open beta of its AI-native workspace that unifies CRM and email into one intelligent system of record. It enriches contacts automatically from emails, calendars, and social activity, transcribes meetings, updates pipelines, and converts emails into tasks seamlessly. Small teams and founders can sign up for free to leverage this for enhanced productivity.

items.title: Build Custom AI Tools with Claude to Replace SaaS and Save Costs for Small Brands
items.summary: Ecommerce expert Davie Fogarty explains how small brand owners can use Claude AI to create bespoke tools in one day, ditching expensive SaaS subscriptions. Key builds include competitor social trackers, inventory alerts, margin calculators, review aggregators, creative briefs, and product launch monitors—all without developers via Claude Code. This approach saves thousands monthly while boosting efficiency.
